title: Browsing the cloud from inside Blender

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine you're modeling in Blender, and your whole asset library lives in a cloud bucket. What if you could browse it like a folder, without leaving the program?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds handy. Is that what Antoine built?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He took an existing add-on, credited the original author, and explored it in his fork called bloc. It adds a panel inside Blender for browsing files stored in Amazon S3 or MinIO, which is a self-hosted alternative.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay, but cloud storage doesn't really have folders, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, it only has long names, called keys. Think of a name like models slash chairs slash oak dot O B J. The add-on splits that name on the slashes and builds a nested tree, so the panel shows real-looking folders you can open and close.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clever. And how do you pick which cloud to talk to?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A connection object holds the provider, the endpoint, the bucket and the region. You can save several connections in the preferences and switch the active one. The artist stays in Blender, and the add-on turns each click into the right storage request.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about finding things in a big library?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's fuzzy search. It scores file names and path pieces, puts exact matches first, and has filters for scenes, meshes, images and materials. Typos still find your file.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And when you click an asset?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It downloads to a temporary spot, then Blender's own importer opens it. Formats like S T L, O B J, P L Y and U S D are supported. There's also an option to upload the current blend file back to the bucket.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's a bridge between a graphics tool and a platform service.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly the mix Antoine enjoys. The full write-up has the diagram of the browse and import paths.
